claims.text: Plastic deformation behavior in NiTi shape-memory alloys is strongly temperature-dependent.
The martensitic-to-austenitic transformation alters phase-boundary mobility in NiTi.
The martensitic-to-austenitic transformation alters the distribution of dislocations in NiTi.
The NiTi alloy is primarily martensitic at low temperatures.
Controlled heating across the transformation-temperature range is the proposed intervention.
Mechanical tests will be conducted below Ms, within the transformation regime, and above Af.
In situ high-resolution TEM and digital image correlation will be used during mechanical testing.
The relevant structural mediator is the evolution of martensite-austenite interfaces.
Changes in dislocation density and distribution accompany the evolution of martensite-austenite interfaces.
The temperature-induced phase transformation modifies dislocation nucleation and motion in NiTi.
The austenitic phase has enhanced phase-boundary mobility relative to the martensitic phase.
The austenitic phase has reduced dislocation pinning relative to the martensitic phase.
Enhanced phase-boundary mobility and reduced dislocation pinning lower the yield stress of austenitic NiTi relative to martensitic NiTi.
Above Af, NiTi will have lower yield strength than it has below Ms.
Above Af, NiTi will have greater ductility than it has below Ms.
The more stable martensitic structure below Ms resists plastic deformation.
Predominantly martensitic NiTi at constant low temperature requires higher stress for plastic deformation.
The martensite and austenite start and finish temperatures delineate regimes in which plasticity changes.
The quantitative changes in yield stress and dislocation dynamics may depend on processing history and testing conditions.

Failure to observe either a significant yield-stress decrease or enhanced phase-boundary mobility with corresponding dislocation reorganization across the transformation will falsify the proposed mechanism.
